PullRequest.Title: Keep all Agent Host shell output scrollable in the inline chat terminal
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340226
Stacked on: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340222

- Give the inline chat terminal of an Agent Host output-only shell (`isPty: false`) the Agent Host's terminal content limit as its scrollback, as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340222 does for the Background Shells preview.
- Add a `scrollback` parameter to `DetachedTerminalSnapshotMirror` and forward it to `createDetachedTerminal`. Every other chat terminal mirror keeps `terminal.integrated.scrollback`.
- The inline terminal always received the full output, but it kept only 1,000 rows. Scrolled up while output streamed, its oldest rows dropped out from under the view, so it jumped or looked stuck, and the start of the output was gone.
- A scrolled-up view now stays on the lines you scrolled to, and scrolling back to the bottom follows new output again.

### Scope

- Only the inline chat terminal of Agent Host output-only shells. Workbench terminals, client-hosted PTY shells, and local command mirrors are unchanged.

### Manual test

1. Save this as `stream.py` in a folder:

   ```python
   import time

   # Long lines, one every 0.15s: passes the 8 KiB large-output limit after ~50 lines.
   for i in range(2000):
       print(f"[main] request {i:03d} served from vscode-file://vscode-app/out/vs/code/electron-main/main.js " + "x" * 80, flush=True)
       time.sleep(0.15)
   ```

2. Open the folder in the Agents window and send this in a Copilot chat:

   ```text
   Start `python3 stream.py` in this workspace as an async background shell (attached, not detached). Do not wait for it or read its output; just reply "started".
   ```

3. Expand the `python3 stream.py` tool call to show its inline terminal.
4. After `request 600`, scroll up inside the inline terminal while output streams. The view should stay on the lines you scrolled to instead of jumping.
5. Scroll to the top. It should reach `request 000`. Before this change it stops about 1,000 rows back.
6. Scroll back to the bottom. It should follow new output again.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/chatTerminalCommandMirror.test.ts`: 137 passing. The new test fails without the scrollback change.
- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on the changed files: passed.
- `npm run precommit` (hygiene): passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the files this PR changes. Locally it still reports errors elsewhere from my SDK install, which has no type declarations, and a missing `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`, so CI covers the full check.
- Code OSS with `stream.py`, before this change: scrolled to the bottom, the inline terminal showed `request 1997` to `1999`, so no output was missing, but its top was `request 1664`. With this change, checked by hand that it scrolls back through the whole run and stays put while scrolled up.

</details>

-----------------------------------------
<details>
<summary>Inspirations from</summary>

- The scrollback value, and why it covers everything the host keeps, comes from the Background Shells preview in #340222: [`BackgroundShellOutputView`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/abcbbcc5de6657b7ed27b5d9db1f4cffcca436d5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/sessionBackgroundShellOutputView.ts#L146-L147).
- Detecting Agent Host output-only terminals by `isPty === false` follows the [retained output check](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/abcbbcc5de6657b7ed27b5d9db1f4cffcca436d5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L421-L424) and the [`isPty` contract](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/abcbbcc5de6657b7ed27b5d9db1f4cffcca436d5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatService.ts#L744-L745).
- The mirror forwards its value to the [`IDetachedXTermOptions.scrollback`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/abcbbcc5de6657b7ed27b5d9db1f4cffcca436d5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminal.ts#L444-L445) option that #340222 added.

</details>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The uncapped append, independent bounded terminal store, background continuation path, and non-clearing finalize lifecycle are explicit. Output volume prevalence affects severity exposure, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host heap bytes held by the cumulative JavaScript string, plus allocation/GC work as it grows.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows linearly with total output over the full lifetime of each chunk-streamed shell and adds across concurrently or historically retained background shells, rather than staying near the 100,000-character terminal cap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory and increasing GC pressure, potentially exhausting the Agent Host on long-lived log-producing commands.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The partial-result path replaced lastSnapshot with the runtime's throttled cumulative snapshot, which the surrounding contract documents as becoming a rolling tail after the large-output threshold; the terminal manager separately trims retained terminal content at 100,000 characters.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Chunk mode concatenates every ANSI-stripped output chunk into stream.lastSnapshot without applying the terminal manager's rolling content limit.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 334 introduces cumulative concatenation of every streamed chunk into lastSnapshot, creating a second retained transcript that bypasses AGENT_HOST_TERMINAL_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH.
Findings.Title: Bound the transcript retained for chunked shells
Findings.Impact: A noisy or long-running background shell can make the Agent Host retain its entire output indefinitely, causing steadily increasing heap use and GC pressure even though the visible terminal state is bounded.
Findings.Evidence: appendChunk executes stream.lastSnapshot += text for every tool.shell_output event. AgentHostTerminalManager trims its own content to 80,000 after crossing 100,000, but that does not affect lastSnapshot. Background calls continue through isStreamingInBackground; completeBackgroundShell only finalizes the stream, and _finalize does not clear lastSnapshot or remove the map entry, so the full transcript remains until the chat/session is disposed.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep only a rolling suffix matching the terminal manager's cap and clear comparison state when the stream finalizes; if completion reconciliation needs whole-output equality, maintain bounded metadata such as length plus an incremental digest instead of the full transcript.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed value, 100× default ratio, xterm option propagation, schema's explicit preallocation behavior, and mirror lifetime are all directly established in repository code; only the exact bytes per row vary by xterm implementation.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Preallocated xterm scrollback rows and terminal cell-buffer memory.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The reserved row capacity increases 100× at the default configuration for each created mirror and scales with the number of tool outputs the user has ever expanded in the rendered chat.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Substantially increased retained renderer memory and GC pressure, with possible renderer slowdown or out-of-memory failures in chats containing several expanded shell outputs.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: These mirrors inherited terminal.integrated.scrollback, whose default is 1,000 rows, so opening a small output did not reserve a 100,000-row buffer.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every Agent Host output-only terminal snapshot now creates its detached xterm with a 100,000-row scrollback override, even when the command produced only a few lines.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 439 changes Agent Host output-only mirrors from the configured scrollback (normally 1,000 rows) to AGENT_HOST_TERMINAL_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (100,000), despite that constant being defined in characters rather than rows.
Findings.Title: Size scrollback from actual output instead of preallocating 100,000 rows
Findings.Impact: Expanding ordinary shell output can cause a large renderer-memory spike and GC pressure; the cost multiplies across tool blocks because collapsing a ChatTerminalToolOutputSection does not dispose its snapshot mirror.
Findings.Evidence: The added callback returns AGENT_HOST_TERMINAL_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (100,000 characters) as xterm's row-count option. The repository's terminal.integrated.scrollback schema explicitly says xterm pre-allocates memory based on this value and defaults to 1,000. DetachedTerminalSnapshotMirror forwards the value to createDetachedTerminal, while toggle(false) only hides the output and leaves _snapshotMirror registered for the part's lifetime. The same character-to-row override is also used by BackgroundShellOutputView.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not pass the character cap directly as a row capacity. Size scrollback from the snapshot's actual wrapped row count (and grow it as retained output grows), and release/recreate the detached mirror on collapse so small and hidden outputs do not retain worst-case capacity.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The old throttled contract and new one-call-per-chunk path through synchronous envelope broadcast to transport.send are directly traceable. Runtime chunk size affects magnitude but not the fan-out mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: ANSI-processing CPU, action/envelope allocations, protocol transport sends, serialized message bytes, and downstream xterm writes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Work scales with raw SDK chunk count times the number of subscribed clients and active chunk-streamed shells; processing is synchronous and serialized per event, with no coalescing to bound bursts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC and CPU overhead, lower output throughput, and possible dropped frames in clients rendering noisy shell output.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing path consumed explicitly throttled cumulative tool.execution_partial_result snapshots and emitted only each snapshot's unseen suffix, so update frequency was bounded by snapshot throttling rather than raw process chunk frequency.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each tool.shell_output chunk is processed and immediately appended to the terminal manager, producing a separate TerminalData action and protocol notification.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 333 places appendOutputTerminalData directly in the per-chunk handler, converting every newly handled raw shell chunk into its own state/protocol update.
Findings.Title: Coalesce raw shell chunks before broadcasting terminal updates
Findings.Impact: High-volume commands can flood the Agent Host event loop and subscribed clients with small terminal messages, reducing shell/chat throughput and causing renderer work or jank while output streams.
Findings.Evidence: The new onToolShellOutput listener calls appendChunk for every SDK event. This line calls appendOutputTerminalData once per accepted chunk; that method synchronously dispatches a TerminalData action. AgentHostStateManager emits an envelope, ProtocolServerHandler adds it to the replay buffer and calls transport.send for every relevant client, with no batching, timer, queue limit, or backpressure in this path.
Findings.Recommendation: Buffer processed text per tool call and flush ordered batches on a short scheduler or size threshold, with explicit flushes before completion/finalization and disposal so ordering and final output are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Foreground Agent Host output-only shell streaming into an inline chat terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each SDK tool.shell_output event is synchronously normalized, appended to the output terminal, emitted as TerminalData, and broadcast before that chunk can appear in a subscribed client. Tool completion itself is separate, but an output burst competes on the same Agent Host event loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast a JSON-RPC TerminalData action through each relevant client's protocol transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport send per accepted raw shell chunk per relevant client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only throttled tool.execution_partial_result snapshots were handled, and each appended the unseen suffix once per snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for live output delivery and synchronous on the Agent Host event path; bursts consume event-loop and client rendering capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a spilled output file at shell completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one bounded read for a completion carrying outputFilePath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion-time spill read already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion publication waits for it when present, but it is not on the per-chunk streaming path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist spilled terminal output to the session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one store per spilled shell completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion-time database store already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion publication waits for the store when output is spilled; unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Raw runtime chunk count and byte volume, multiplied by the number of relevant subscribed clients; unlike the prior throttled cumulative snapshots, effective cardinality is one update per accepted chunk.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are handled synchronously and serialized; there is no batching, limiter, queue bound, or backpressure before protocol broadcast.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing serves repeated chunks. Sequence numbers deduplicate retransmitted/older chunks, but every new sequence is processed and forwarded separately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff's event listener, append path, synchronous state envelope, and per-client transport send are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK chunk sizes and subscriber counts vary, so exact throughput loss is workload-dependent; noisy shell commands remain a realistic burst trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff introduces uncoalesced per-chunk protocol fan-out and an uncapped secondary transcript.

Scenarios.Scenario: Long-running attached shell continuing in the background after its tool call returns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: While the process runs, every new shell chunk follows the same normalization and protocol path. The new lastSnapshot accumulation is not needed for terminal progress and sits off the display critical path, but it remains live for the shell and after finalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send each background shell chunk as an individual TerminalData protocol action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per raw chunk per subscribed client for the full background runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Background output arrived through throttled cumulative snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed for live viewers, but lack of coalescing makes noisy output contend with other Agent Host and renderer work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total bytes emitted over shell lifetime and the number of simultaneous or completed background shells retained by the chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each shell's events are sequential by sequence number, while multiple shells can interleave on the same event loop; no aggregate memory or message-rate limit exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Terminal content has a 100,000-character rolling cap, but lastSnapshot is a separate uncapped copy. Finalization neither evicts nor clears it; disposal occurs with the chat/session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: lastSnapshot += text is uncapped, the terminal manager's cap is independent, and completeBackgroundShell only finalizes without deleting the stream.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Shell duration and log rate vary; servers, watchers, and test loops can realistically emit output for hours.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: retained memory grows with lifetime output despite the host's intended rolling cap, and remains after shell finalization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expanding and collapsing Agent Host shell output in an inline chat tool block
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On first expansion, ChatTerminalToolOutputSection creates and attaches a DetachedTerminalSnapshotMirror before showing the expanded state; xterm construction uses the new scrollback override.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of tool outputs ever expanded in the rendered chat. The 100,000-row capacity applies even to tiny snapshots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation is asynchronous per expansion, but each created mirror remains owned by its output section; collapsing does not dispose it, so costs accumulate rather than being concurrency-limited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The mirror is reused on later expansions, which avoids repeat construction but retains its preallocated buffer while collapsed. There is no size-sensitive allocation keyed to actual output rows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the override is 100,000 versus the 1,000-row default, the configuration schema explicitly documents preallocation by this value, and collapse leaves _snapshotMirror alive.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact bytes per preallocated row depend on xterm internals, but the 100× capacity increase and per-expanded-block lifetime are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: ordinary expansion now reserves worst-case scrollback memory, multiplied across retained tool blocks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a running shell's output from the Background Shells picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening details lazily creates a detached xterm and applies the same 100,000-row override before rendering live output; closing the picker disposes the view.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One currently opened background-shell details view, with repeated opens recreating the terminal; retained output text is capped upstream but the row capacity is set from the character cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The picker generally exposes one details view at a time and disposes it on close, limiting simultaneous instances, but each open still pays the large allocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No warm terminal cache is retained across close/open; each open is a cold detached-terminal creation and each close releases it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lazy construction and close-time disposal are explicit, as is the 100,000-row option.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The temporary memory spike depends on xterm's row representation and allocator behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported character-versus-row preallocation bug affects this path, though its lifecycle bounds simultaneous retention better than inline tool blocks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Regular PTY terminals and non-Agent-Host chat terminal mirrors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Terminal creation and configuration updates continue to use terminal.integrated.scrollback because the new override is undefined.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normal terminal count and configured scrollback; unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing terminal creation and update behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior; the optional override falls back to configuration and remains stable across configuration updates only when explicitly supplied.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the nullish fallback in XtermTerminal and the isPty === false gate.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on this scenario; it confirms the findings are limited to Agent Host output-only terminals.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files. Reported three diff-caused issues: worst-case xterm row preallocation for small outputs, unbounded chunk-transcript retention, and uncoalesced per-chunk protocol fan-out. Checked foreground/background shell lifecycles, inline and picker rendering, protocol IPC, completion-time filesystem/database work, cache behavior, and concurrency. No qualifying shipped-regression fix was established for report_regression_fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
